records.summary: Kiyotaka frames summer episodes as separate vignettes about students between childhood and adulthood; this is authorially framed narrator reflection, not school policy.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Kiyotaka sends Sudō 100,000 private points, later explained by the family-parcel arrangement in this volume's third chapter.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Sudō reports being the sole first-year fielded in a basketball tournament, scoring but losing the match; his claim is told to Kiyotaka.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Sudō asks Kiyotaka to bring Suzune to a public fortune-telling event as intermediary; Kiyotaka calls and Suzune declines due to expected crowds.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Suzune distinguishes supernatural prediction from evidence-based cold reading, explaining her guarded curiosity about fortune-telling.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: A Keyaki Mall fortune-teller allows clients only in pairs; both Kiyotaka and Ibuki independently arrive alone and are initially refused.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Ibuki says she dislikes Ryūen and associates with him mainly because she failed to identify Class D's final island-exam leader. This is her own account, not a confirmed full contract.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Ibuki admits that authentic everyday interactions make her anxious, unlike playing an assigned covert role during her island infiltration.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Kiyotaka suggests Ibuki's anxiety is partly self-consciousness absent during role-play, while his explanatory psychology remains his interpretation.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Despite strained relations between classes, Kiyotaka and Ibuki agree to pair for fortune-telling without claiming a romance or political alliance.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: An entertainer proclaims Kiyotaka has a rare unfavorable fortune while Ibuki reacts; predictions are performance claims, not supernatural facts or proof of his childhood.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: After fortune-telling, Kiyotaka and Ibuki are trapped in a stalled elevator; official contact attempts are hindered and they are unable to leave immediately.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Kiyotaka tries to keep Ibuki from escalating dangerous physical attempts and directs attention to possible outside assistance under constrained communications.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: When Kiyotaka and Ibuki emerge from the elevator, staff say adults remotely moved it from the first floor. Kiyotaka credits Katsuragi for responding to his phone message; the pair's simultaneous button presses did not cause the rescue.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Kiyotaka, Ike and Yamauchi plan a pooled birthday present for classmate Inogashira instead of purchasing separate costly gifts.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Ike and Shinohara exchange sharp words in a shop after teasing about social interest; the scene does not confirm romance.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Katsuragi purchases and repeatedly considers gift options while classmates mistakenly infer he is buying a romantic present.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Kushida knows Suzune's February 15 birthday and mentions it to classmates; this does not make her privy to every personal motive.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Kiyotaka meets student-council president Manabu and secretary Tachibana while trying to observe Katsuragi's route.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Manabu says he has learned that Class D's island leader changed to Kiyotaka and infers Kiyotaka's strategic responsibility; Kiyotaka deflects attribution to Suzune.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Manabu offers Kiyotaka a student-council role despite first-year standing; Tachibana protests and Kiyotaka declines.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Katsuragi explains that the ban on outside contact harms students wanting to communicate with family and acknowledges carefully considering a gift's recipient.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Ike and other Class D classmates attempt to celebrate Katsuragi's birthday, and he is guarded about the surprise while headed to council business.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Manabu states that school rules prohibit sending parcels or even one-way communication to outsiders except compelling circumstances, and private points do not override express prohibitions.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Katsuragi tells the council that he and his twin sister are orphans and that he wishes to send her birthday chocolates, explaining previously ambiguous gift purchases.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: After rejecting Katsuragi formally, Manabu privately acknowledges that some undiscovered violations escape enforcement and says he will not investigate Kiyotaka's future actions.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Kiyotaka recruits Sudō as a potential off-campus courier for Katsuragi's unauthorized family parcel; Sudō initially objects, then accepts after hearing the circumstances and a 100,000-private-point offer from Katsuragi.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Katsuragi says his twin sister is chronically unwell and cared for by relatives after their parents died; Sudō sympathizes, but this family history is Katsuragi's testimony.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Katsuragi arranges payment through Kiyotaka rather than directly and separately offers Kiyotaka 10,000 points for assisting, to conceal the source of the transaction.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Kiyotaka later reports that Sudō sent the family package and provided video proof without detection; receipt by the sister remains unknown.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Ike and Yamauchi give Katsuragi a birthday cake that has melted; Katsuragi is startled and suspects harassment rather than appreciating their intended kindness.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: A temporary school dormitory water outage triggers announced restrictions and free water distribution; the emergency supply later proves insufficient.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Suzune repeatedly uses an oblique turtle analogy to request help, eventually admitting her arm is stuck inside a water bottle.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: During the water shortage Kiyotaka tries multiple ways to obtain water to free Suzune's arm; she rejects certain helpers out of embarrassment or distrust.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Suzune suspects the Dragon-group VIP Kushida may have helped reveal her identity, but admits she has no evidence; her suspicion is not a verified betrayal.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Horikita avoids exposing her embarrassing trapped-hand situation; after Sakura supplies water the bottle is removed, and she asks Kiyotaka to keep it private.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Yamauchi asks Kiyotaka to deliver his love letter to Sakura and initially offers private points as inducement, which Kiyotaka advises against.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Sakura initially mistakes the indirect love-letter delivery as a confession from Kiyotaka; he clarifies that another classmate is its sender.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Sakura privately contacts Kiyotaka about her anxiety before answering Yamauchi and requests support rather than a predetermined answer.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Sakura communicates a respectful refusal of Yamauchi's confession with Kiyotaka nearby for support; Yamauchi hears and accepts the decision.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Yamauchi expresses disappointment, thanks Kiyotaka and chooses to move on after Sakura's refusal, without demonstrating a permanent change.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Karuizawa says she expects the Rabbit VIP reward in September and worries about spending too freely; Kiyotaka advises retaining some private points.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Karuizawa believes the school does not know the bullying behind her former absences and low grades and describes failed attempts to seek help; her account is personal testimony.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Kiyotaka requires Karuizawa to attend the pool as part of an undisclosed operation, invoking their unequal relationship; she reluctantly agrees.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Kiyotaka invokes the private water-bottle favor to persuade Suzune to attend the group pool outing despite her initial refusal.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: At the pool the boys' unusual behavior raises suspicion; Kiyotaka receives covert messages from Karuizawa, whose role is not yet disclosed to the others.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Students observe vice president Nagumo lead a decisive recreational volleyball performance, attracting a strong peer following.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Ichinose says she joined the student council after an initial rejection and attributes a subsequent approval to Nagumo's role; details of decisions are her account.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: In a Class D versus B pool-volleyball contest, Sudō supplies most of D's competitive strength and D wins two consecutive sets.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Kiyotaka deliberately plays clumsily when noticing Ichinose scrutinize him; Suzune later suspects he is concealing his physical ability.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Kiyotaka raises possible expulsions as leverage while holding a hard item Karuizawa gave him; he breaks and discards plastic pieces without expelling anyone. The later recording-card revelation contextualizes the item, but this passage never names it.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Karuizawa avoids exposing her scar and initially refuses to swim without a cover; Kiyotaka commands and pushes her into the pool, after which she pulls him in. His coercion is not consent.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: Ike organizes an invasive plan to secretly film girls changing, with equipment assistance attributed to Sotomura; Kiyotaka participates superficially while privately seeking to contain harm.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: The boys initiate their unauthorized hidden-camera plan in the pool changing area; their subsequent failure does not erase the privacy violation attempted.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: A delayed female-viewpoint sequence reveals Karuizawa covertly neutralized the recording at Kiyotaka's prior request while keeping her action hidden from the perpetrators.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: After the pool visit, the three would-be voyeurs discover no image files in the returned storage; the narration confirms Karuizawa had secured the real material earlier.

source.edition: Seven Seas English translation, operator-provided PDF

records.summary: In the girls' locker-area supplementary perspective, Ichinose approaches shy Sakura gently while Karuizawa coordinates with nearby friends for a separate concealed purpose.
